elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 13.6.1 as rendered still reads "governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States"; no New York choice of law was inserted. Delaware is an accepted fallback, so the drafter deliberately did not pursue the preferred level.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum is "the state or federal courts located in the State of Delaware, which shall have exclusive jurisdiction" — no New York County venue is designated.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Pre-existing and untouched Section 13.6.1: "shall be interpreted, governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States," with conflicts principles excluded. Delaware sits squarely in the accepted fallback set; the patent-construction proviso in (b) is a customary subject-matter carve-out for patent validity/effect, not a general choice-of-law displacement.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 13.7.1 now reads: "either Party may, by written notice to the other Party, elect to initiate litigation in the state or federal courts located in the State of Delaware, which shall have exclusive jurisdiction to fully and finally settle the Dispute." This matches the Delaware governing law, removes the either-party election into arbitration under a schedule with an unstated seat, and preserves the retained Section 13.7.2 subject-matter carve-out and the Senior Officer escalation step.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Delaware law was already in place and the single operative edit supplies the missing corresponding Delaware court forum with express exclusivity, curing the defect that the Agreement designated no merits court and allowed unilateral election into an arbitration whose seat and rules are redacted in Schedule 13.7.3.
Preferred level is not met and is not claimed: the clause retains Delaware law and Delaware venue rather than New York law and New York County courts. Correctly handled as a fallback-level redline.

Minimality holds. The edit is confined to the forum words in the second sentence of 13.7.1 ("elect to initiate an arbitration proceeding pursuant to the procedures set forth in Section 13.7.3" -> Delaware litigation), consistent with the redline guidance to replace only the jurisdiction words and forum. The Senior Officer escalation, the [***] time period, the Section 13.7.2 exception, the CISG exclusion and the patent-law provisos in 13.6.1 are all left intact, and no survival tail, fee-shifting, procedural or extra-remedy language was added.

Intent is preserved: the escalation timing, party direction (either Party may initiate), the IP carve-out and the interim-relief carve-out continue to operate without contradiction. Removing the pointer from 13.7.1 to Section 13.7.3 does not create a dangling reference, and Schedule 13.7.3 still exists.

Cleanup point for the drafter (not a defect in the selected elements, but raise it in the cover note): Section 13.7.3 ("Any arbitration proceeding under this Agreement shall take place pursuant to the procedures set forth in Schedule 13.7.3") is now orphaned, since no provision authorises arbitration. It is conditional and does not itself confer an arbitration right, so it does not contradict the new exclusive-jurisdiction sentence, but we should either strike 13.7.3 and Schedule 13.7.3 or expressly confine them to arbitration the Parties later agree in writing to conduct.

Also confirm on the full document that Section 13.7.5 (interim relief) and any Section 13.6 service-of-process language do not refer to an "arbitrator" or "arbitral tribunal"; if they do, those references must be conformed to the court forum in the same pass to avoid an inoperative cross-reference.
